chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Al-Fudayl and Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Humran, that he asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Surely We revealed it on a blessed night.' He said: 'Yes, the Night of Pre-determination. And it is in every year in the month of Ramadan, in the last ten days. So the Quran was not revealed except during the Night of Pre-determination.'
Therein every wise affair is made distinct

He said: 'It is ordained during the Night of Pre-determination, everything that occurs in that year up to its like from the coming year, good and evil, obedience and disobedience, offspring, lifespan, or livelihood. So whatever is determined in that year and decreed, it is inevitable, and for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, therein is the Will.'
The Night of Predestination is better than a thousand months

I said, 'Which thing is meant by that?' So he said: 'The righteous deeds therein, from the Prayer, and the Zakat, and the varieties of goodness, are better than the deed during a thousand months wherein is not the Night of Pre-determination. And, had Allah, Blessed and High, not multiplied it for the believers, they would not have reached (success). But, Allah multiplies the good deeds for them through our love.'

key_terms.بِحُبِّنَا: Through our love (referring to the Imams/Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ: The Night of Pre-determination, a specific night in Ramadan

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Laylat al-Qadr and how are deeds multiplied on this night?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the theological concept of *Taqdir* (annual decree), where specific events such as lifespan and sustenance are determined for the coming year. It highlights the unique merit of Laylat al-Qadr by linking the multiplication of rewards not just to worship, but specifically to the love of the Ahl al-Bayt, a key tenet in Shia jurisprudence. The narration further clarifies that while decrees are made, they remain subject to Allah's will, balancing predestination with divine agency.
